newsitem.title: USA: Toyota N. American production up 5.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Toyota N. American production up 5.4 pct.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Tuesday that its North American production for the first two months of 1997 totaled 140,270 cars and trucks, up 5.4 percent from the same period of 1996.
Toyota's Georgetown, Ky., plant built 73,196 Camry and Avalon cars in the first two months of 1997, an increase of 5.6 percent from a year earlier.

The company said its New United Motor Manufacturing Inc joint venture with General Motors Corp in Fremont, Calif., built 50,550 Corolla cars and compact pickup trucks in January and February, up 7.1 percent from a year earlier.

Toyota Motor Corporate Services of North America Inc. also said the automaker's Canadian plant in Cambridge, Ontario, built 16,524 Corolla cars in January and February, down 0.5 percent from the same period of 1996.

Toyota said that 63.2 percent of the vehicles Toyota sold in the United States during February were produced in the company's North American factories. It has achieved a 60 percent North American sales mix nearly every month since March 1996.

Toyota said the domestic content of its North American-built cars and trucks is currently 70 percent or more, according the the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency method of calculation, which includes labor.
The new Sienna minivan, which will begin production in the fall of 1997 at the Georgetown plant, will contain about 75 percent domestic content, Toyota said.
